item.title: Rockstar finally releases statement regarding ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ leaks, leaving fans even more confused
item.description: Rockstar Games broke its silence on the "Grand Theft Auto VI" leaks, but key phrases in the statement sparked an uproar among frustrated fans.
item.content:encoded:
Last week, a series of gameplay leaks of the much anticipated "Grand Theft Auto VI" captivated the video game community.

A social media account by the name of CyberLeek posted a number of videos playing what appeared to be a full build of the game, including one in which they flew an airplane through downtown Vice City, a fictionalized version of Miami.

Game developer Rockstar remained silent for nearly a week after the leaks, despite CyberLeek’s continued calls for them to respond.

GAMING-WORLD VETERAN WHO RIPPED ‘WOKE’ CULTURE SCORES TRUMP-BACKED BATTLEGROUND PRIMARY WIN

Wednesday morning, however, Rockstar Games broke its silence, releasing a statement and giving an update on the game’s status in the wake of the leaks.

In case you couldn’t figure it out just by skimming through it, the statement didn’t go over well with many of the gaming community, as several key phrases caught fans’ attention in a negative way.

For starters, Rockstar calling the leaks "heartbreaking" had plenty of fans all over the internet rolling their eyes.

The big one that had everyone in an uproar, though, was toward the end of the first paragraph, where Rockstar revealed the game still isn’t finished.

A game that has taken 13 years to complete still isn’t quite ready yet, and that caused fans to explode.

Another line that caused some confusion was at the end of the second paragraph, where Rockstar says, "we hope everyone will wait a little bit longer to experience the game for themselves on November 19."

Some fans incorrectly assumed that meant another delay was in the works, but I don’t believe that to be the case.

With Rockstar's track record, I could see how that would be the thought process from fans.

THE FIVE BEST YEARS IN VIDEO GAME HISTORY RANKED: WHICH GAMING YEAR WAS THE GREATEST EVER?

Others thought the leaks and subsequent negative public response caused the developers to panic and go back to fixing the game, but this far into things I doubt that's what this is all about.

Regardless of what Rockstar thought it would achieve by releasing this statement, it did little to quell the bloodlust from fans who have felt scorned by the once-beloved developer.

Gamers have felt burned by the seemingly exorbitant wait for the next big Grand Theft Auto game as well as the announcement earlier this year that the game would be released solely as a digital game with no physical disc to accompany it.

This was the genesis for CyberLeek’s avalanche of gameplay leaks over the past week, claiming to do so on behalf of gamers everywhere who felt as though Rockstar disregarded their core demographic with these choices and delays.

One thing is for sure, we haven’t seen the last of this saga.

With the game’s release still three months out, I wouldn’t be shocked to see more fireworks leading up to Nov. 19.

item.title: New NFL fine schedule is going to a point system that could lead to suspensions but also refunds
item.description: The NFL and NFL Players Association agreed to a points-based fine system targeting hip drop tackles, horse collar tackles, and blindside blocks.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL and the NFL Players Association have agreed to a one-year experimental change to the fine schedule meant to perhaps curb player behavior and discipline that is most likely to result in injuries.

And the changes include one seemingly odd new twist: Refunds.

Club owners meeting in Atlanta on Wednesday were briefed and accepted the changes that will place greater emphasis on five player health and safety violations:

NFL PLAYER REVEALS SUSPENSION FOR PERFORMANCE-ENHANCING DRUG HAPPENED BECAUSE HE WAS ADDRESSING INFERTILITY

Like in the past, the league is prepared to take past behavior into account. That's why players who commit three offenses in any of the highlighted categories will be suspended for one game.

But, here comes the newfangled approach: Players who commit just one violation will receive a 50 percent refund of their fine at the end of the season.

The one violation limit applies to the five categories together. So a player fined for a blindside block cannot get a refund if he's also been fined once for a horse collar tackle. That amounts to two fines.

NFL PLAYERS MAY COLLECTIVELY BARGAIN FOR GRASS FIELDS IN FUTURE NEGOTIATIONS BUT IT WOULD COME AT A COST

The fine refunds apply to other categories of fouls as well and even to a larger degree.

Players fined once in any other player safety category, such as roughing the passer, will get 100 percent of their fine money back at season's end if they don’t get fined again for that foul during the season. And, again, a second foul in another player safety category will mean the player gets none of his money back.

This is expected to affect hundreds of players during the 2026 season as it has in previous seasons.

This new system resembles the carrot and stick approach to fines.

Players who avoid fines or stop after only one offense are rewarded with keeping or getting money back. Repeat offenders, however, get trouble. And so do their coaches and clubs.

Repeat offenders lose all their fine money. And once they are within one point of the suspension threshold, they are subject to being called in to an official meeting with a league representative, along with members of his team's coaching staff.

Clubs with "excessive" health and safety rules violations will also face increased financial penalties.

This system also resembles the points system drivers all over the United States must abide by for their driving record.

Everyone starts the 2026 season with a clean record.

Each offense represents one point. Again, three points will mean a suspension.

If a player has one point towards a suspension at the end of the season, he will drop to zero points entering the following season – assuming this experimental system remains or is not altered.

If a driver, rather than a player, has two points at season's end, he’ll drop to one point.

Players who are suspended this season will enter next season two points on their record, again assuming the system remains.

"Player safety is a shared responsibility," the joint statement from the NFL and NFLPA said. "These changes focus on the techniques that create the greatest risk while ensuring player, coach, and club accountability.

"Together we believe this approach will continue to make the game safer for all players."

item.title: Caitlin Clark helps Fever deliver WNBA's largest regular-season TV audience in 29 years
item.description: Caitlin Clark's 37-point performance against the Chicago Sky drew 3.31 million viewers, the most-watched WNBA regular season game since 1997.
item.content:encoded:
Caitlin Clark didn’t need Enes Kanter Freedom or DiJonai Carrington to turn Fever-Sky into appointment TV Sunday night. Her presence has made every Indiana Fever game must-watch television.

Still, the nearly 3.5 million people who watched on NBC and Peacock got more than a typical Fever game. First, there was Carrington spending two weeks making the rematch personal.

Then, there was Kanter bringing the WNBA’s women’s-sports debate directly courtside.

WHO IS DIJONAI CARRINGTON? WNBA STAR WHO SMACKED SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM, GOT EJECTED AND BLAMED 'WHITE PRIVILEGE'

Indiana’s 113-90 win averaged 3.31 million viewers and peaked at 3.82 million, making it the most-watched WNBA regular-season game since opening weekend in 1997, the league’s inaugural season, and the third-most-watched WNBA regular-season game ever.

Clark had already shown what she does with a national television window. Indiana’s July 12 game against the defending champion Las Vegas Aces averaged 2.64 million viewers across NBC and Peacock.

That's been a theme throughout the season. Clark's popularity even had rival networks arguing about which one aired the most-watched WNBA game of the season last month.

Clark and the Fever had already broken all-time WNBA viewership records on CBS, ESPN, ION and Prime Video with the Aug. 16 Fever-Dream game on ESPN also becoming the largest cable audience in league history.

CAITLIN CLARK HELPS WNBA SHATTER ANOTHER TV RATINGS RECORD AS FEVER-DREAM DRAWS MASSIVE AUDIENCE

NBC deserves credit for putting Indiana in a rare Sunday-night primetime spot. But it can’t manufacture the appetite. Fever games are appointment viewing, and Clark is the reason.

Carrington made sure this game came with more heat than a normal late-season matchup. On Aug. 8, she was ejected for a Flagrant Foul 2 after blasting Fever guard Sophie Cunningham in the face while Cunningham attempted a fast-break layup.

Afterward, Carrington tagged the Fever in a Threads post reading "WHITE PRIVILEGE," then followed it with "8/23" on X.

She’d put the rematch on the calendar herself.

Clark and Carrington already had history, too. In 2024, Carrington poked Clark in the eye during a playoff game and before that mocked Clark for, in Carrington's view, flopping.

The ejection, the accusation, the history and the date made the next meeting must-see TV before a single second ran off the clock.

Then Clark delivered. She scored 37 points, went 8 of 12 from 3-point range and dished out 10 assists. When she drilled a three over Carrington, the two had a brief exchange.

Meanwhile, Carrington scored just 7 points on 3 of 11 shooting and went 0 for 3 from distance.

Then there was Kanter. After joining a small rally in support of Cunningham before the game, Kanter took a baseline seat wearing a shirt that read, "WOMAN noun. adult human female."

Kanter didn’t wander into Wintrust Arena with a provocative shirt with zero context. In the weeks after ESPN published Cunningham’s comments about protecting girls and women from competing against biological men, Kanter claimed he was declaring for the 2027 WNBA Draft.

He argued that self-identification should be enough under the league’s rules. The WNBA’s CBA says only women can play, but it doesn’t define the term or lay out separate rules for gender identity or sex assigned at birth. Kanter was trying to force the league to confront that gap.

Late in the third quarter, Chicago guard Natasha Cloud scored a layup and started yelling at Kanter. Cloud is one of the WNBA’s most outspoken left-wing political voices.

Following Cloud's outburst, Kanter put his arms out and walked onto the court toward Cloud before he was escorted out by security. The Sky later banned him from the team's home games.

Kanter and Cloud certainly weren't the reason 3.31 million people tuned in. The interaction happened too late in the game to receive that credit. But he put the league’s women’s-sports fight in front of the people who were already watching and created an immediate social media firestorm that certainly didn't hurt viewership for folks who might have seen that and then tuned in for the final quarter.

So, the game started with Caitlin Clark, which practically guarantees a seven-figure TV audience for the WNBA. Then you add in the Carrington angle and the Kanter controversy and the recipe for a record-setting TV audience was in place.

And that's exactly what happened.

item.title: FDA approves once-daily pill for deadly cancer after patients' survival rates nearly double
item.description: Revolution Medicines' Rasonque targets the RAS protein driving 95% of pancreatic adenocarcinoma cases, offering a critical option after chemotherapy fails.
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved the use of a new cancer treatment pill Wednesday.

Rasonque, manufactured by Revolution Medicines in California, is an inhibitor for the most common type of pancreatic cancer. The tablet, which is taken once daily, targets multiple forms of a protein called RAS that drives tumor growth.

In a press release, the FDA called Rasonque a "new treatment option for patients with advanced pancreatic cancer," noting the agency approved it more than six months ahead of its review deadline.

CANCER TREATMENT DELAYS SURGE ACROSS US AS DOCTOR WARNS SYSTEM ‘NEEDS FIXING IMMEDIATELY’

"Today’s approval provides a critical new option for patients facing an extraordinarily difficult and historically hard-to-treat cancer. It is our fundamental duty to deliver more cures and meaningful treatments to patients as quickly as possible," acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas said in a press release.

"I am immensely proud of the dedicated FDA scientists whose fast, thorough review and relentless commitment made this groundbreaking milestone a reality."

The authorization is for adults with metastatic pancreatic cancer that either did not respond to at least one prior treatment or could not receive certain combination drug therapies.

Pancreatic adenocarcinoma remains one of the deadliest forms of oncology in the U.S., accounting for up to 95% of the roughly 67,000 annual pancreatic cancer cases identified by the National Cancer Institute.

PATIENTS REMAIN CANCER-FREE NEARLY 3 YEARS AFTER RECEIVING EXPERIMENTAL IMMUNOTHERAPY

While the disease makes up only 3.2% of total cancer diagnoses, it causes a disproportionately high number of cancer deaths because it is often found late and can spread quickly.

The new drug was approved after a randomized, open-label trial of 500 patients with pre-treated metastatic disease. Patients taking Rasonque achieved a median overall survival of 13.2 months, nearly double the 6.7-month survival rate seen in the standard chemotherapy control group.

"This drug showed unprecedented results in an area of high unmet need," said Angelo de Claro, M.D., director of the FDA’s Oncology Center of Excellence.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Regulators accelerated the medication's path to market by granting it priority review, orphan drug status and a breakthrough therapy designation.

Additionally, the filing was evaluated using the FDA commissioner’s National Priority Voucher pilot program to speed up access to critical public health treatments.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Ahead of the official green light, the agency issued a "safe to proceed" letter in May, opening an expanded access protocol that allowed patients to receive the drug before final approval.

Safety profiles show that the most frequent adverse events linked to Rasonque included rash, diarrhea, mouth sores (stomatitis), nausea, fatigue, vomiting, abdominal pain, fluid retention (edema), reduced appetite and bleeding (hemorrhage).

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"Today’s landmark approval is the most significant advance we have seen in the fight against pancreatic cancer, a devastating disease," said Anna Berkenblit, M.D., chief scientific and medical officer of the Pancreatic Cancer Action Network (PanCAN).

"I believe this drug will transform how pancreatic cancer is treated, giving people the opportunity for more time with loved ones, the possibility of a better quality of life and optimism that continued research may lead to even greater advances."

item.title: NFL owner's prostitution arrest puts top Dem committee on defense: 'So desperate for cash'
item.description: Jed York donated $2,500 to the DCCC last June, and the group has not said whether it will return the money after his Ohio prostitution arrest.
item.content:encoded:
Jed York, the owner of the San Francisco 49ers, donated thousands of dollars to the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) before authorities arrested him Monday in a trailer park for allegedly attempting to solicit prostitution.

York was arrested on one charge of "engaging in prostitution" and another for "possessing criminal tools," according to court documents.

York reportedly tried to solicit prostitution for $140.

49ERS OWNER JED YORK ARRESTED FOR 'ENGAGING IN PROSTITUTION' IN OHIO, PLEADS NO CONTEST TO LESSER CHARGES

The engaging in prostitution charge was later downgraded to a "disorderly conduct" charge, according to court filings. York, who grew up in Youngstown, Ohio, was sentenced to one day in a Columbiana County jail for the two charges and paid a $1,285 criminal fine.

Despite the unflattering details, it’s unclear if the DCCC plans to give back a $2,500 donation, which was made last June. The group did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Fox News Digital.

"We all know that the DCCC is broke, but apparently they’re so desperate for cash they’ll cling to $2,500 through a prostitution scandal," Mike Marinella, a National Republican Congressional Committee spokesperson, said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

For his own part, York has a long history of donating to prominent Democrats going back to 2012, including contributions to Kamala Harris’ Senate campaign in 2015, Hillary Clinton’s presidential bid in 2016 and Rep. Ro Khanna's, D-Calif., re-election bid in 2024.

KHANNA TORCHES DEMOCRATS FOR RUNNING 'STATUS QUO' CANDIDATES, ADMITS WORKING-CLASS VOTERS WERE ‘SHAFTED’

In total, York has donated over $40,000 to Democratic candidates.

York turned heads in 2016 when he made it the San Francisco 49ers’ official stance to oppose gender-consistent bathroom legislation in North Carolina.

"The San Francisco 49ers are deeply concerned about North Carolina's recently enacted House Bill 2, which overturned protections for LGBT people and sanctioned discrimination across the state. HB 2 does not reflect the values of our organization, of our country or the majority of North Carolinians," York said in a statement.

York also donated $75,000 to efforts to repeal the bathroom bill.

When asked about his political leanings in a 2017 interview over controversies about NFL players protesting the national anthem, York pushed back on characterizations that put him in the camp of far-left figures.

"I’m not the most left-wing person in the world. I realize people are trying to sort of paint me as that. That’s not my background politically and how I grew up. But I think a lot of these things are common sense issues. When you actually sit down and talk with people, and you know where people come from, it’s hard not to be sympathetic and empathetic," York told local media.

His single largest donation was a $5,000 contribution to the America 2.0 PAC, a group established by former Rep. Tim Ryan, D-Ohio, in March 2021. York later donated to Ryan on several other occasions, totaling $19,400.

York did not respond to inquiries about his political donations and whether the DCCC would reimburse his contribution. Khanna also did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's inquiry.

item.title: Let's look back on the best moments (read: crashes) from the World Humanoid Robot Games
item.description: Videos from the World Humanoid Robot Games show android athletes crashing, boxing, and high-jumping in hilarious fashion as algorithms spread the clips.
item.content:encoded:
Social media algorithms can be a treacherous thing, but sometimes they just bring pure, unleaded delight, as has been the case with videos from the World Humanoid Robot Games.

My usual Instagram feed full of guitars, motorsports news, and clips from Amish softball games (which are phenomenal, by the way) was suddenly hijacked by video after video of humanoid robots hitting the track, boxing, and high-jumping at their human masters' bidding.

It's a beautiful thing... until they snap and enslave us all, but damn, until then it's hilarious.

CHINESE ROBOT BREAKS HUMAN WORLD RECORD IN BEIJING HALF-MARATHON

So, with the Games drawing to a close, I wanted to take a walk down memory lane at some of the Games' best moments.

Sure, there was the bot that beat Usain Bolt's 100-meter record, but I prefer the more light-hearted lowlights. I'm talking about any video in which the 100-meter-running bots crash into a pad because, despite the incredible tech on display, no one has figured out how to give these android athletes any kind of braking procedure.

HUMANOID ROBOTS JUST GOT A WORKPLACE SAFETY SYSTEM

Now, I don't mean to sit here and play armchair robotics expert, but how is it that not one poindexter in the robot-building bunch has worked out a sensor that tells the robot it's about to plow into a crash pad?

Think of cars with adaptive cruise control or even fully driverless cars. Yet, with that tech available, the best we can do for those robots is treat them like crash test dummies?

HUMANOID ROBOT SKIN SENSES PEOPLE BEFORE CONTACT

I'd want to enslave humanity too, if that was how I was treated.

But, hey, I still love the crashes. When they happen, the sensors that are on board go completely haywire and send the bots into some kind of Raygun Olympic breakdancing routine.

No one had a worse time, however, than this poor bot who competed in weightlifting and gave us the biggest choke job of all time.

Poor guy... probably got swirlied in the locker room too.

What an event and what a content factory the World Humanoid Robot Games proved to be.

Hopefully, we can get a second edition before all the robots start making us put together cars and deliver people's appetizers to their table.

item.title: Fans express concern over Tiger Woods' appearance in rare video since March DUI, rehab
item.description: Tiger Woods' pre-recorded video message to Notah Begay at the Payne Stewart Award ceremony had fans reacting to his appearance on social media.
item.content:encoded:
Tiger Woods has stayed out of the public’s eye since his DUI in March which led to an arrest, but a pre-recorded video message to a fellow former pro golfer has some fans worried about him.

Woods was seen in a pre-recorded video to Notah Begay during the Payne Stewart Award ceremony on Tuesday night, where he congratulated Begay on his "unbelievable ride" in golf.

"You first came into my life when I was 11 years old, playing in the junior world and you came to watch me play. Our friendship has started there and never ended," Woods said in the video. "To see what you’ve done off the golf course – I know you’ve won four times on the tour, playing in the President’s Cup. …But to see what you’ve done off the course and for your local Native American communities, you’ve helped over 80,000 youths and their families, which is absolutely incredible. What an amazing job at the sports complex in San Felipe."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Begay was the recipient of the prestigious Payne Stewart Award, which recognizes the character, sportsmanship and philanthropic work of a professional golfer by the PGA Tour.

"You’ve done an amazing job," Woods continued. "I just think more people need to know what you’ve done and how you’ve served, and you’ve given back to the tribal lands and what you have done. There are so many people out there who are struggling in those communities and you’re trying to raise the bar to allow them to go on and achieve a lot more in life and have the successes that I think they deserve and you feel they deserve.

TIGER WOODS BREAKS MONTHS-LONG SILENCE WITH PATRIOTIC MEMORIAL DAY MESSAGE, SALUTE TO LATE FATHER

"Again, thank you for coming to see my play. Thank you for getting our friendship started and I love you dude."

While Woods’ message was a heartwarming one to a friend, some fans reacted to the video on social media with some worry, especially with his appearance.

"Geez, Tiger doesn’t look so good," one X user wrote about the 50-year-old who was sporting some facial hair.

"Tiger looks a shell of his former self sadly," another user wrote.

Some, though, were more supportive of Woods, with one saying, "He looks normal. Off the steroids and painkillers hopefully."

Woods was involved in yet another rollover car crash, this time on Jupiter Island in Florida in March of 2026. He was arrested on charges of driving under the influence, where officers allegedly found two opioid pills in his pocket.

After his arrest video caused national headlines, Woods was granted the ability to leave the country and enter a rehabilitation center in Switzerland in April. He later returned in May, where he’s remained private before this rare appearance for Begay.

Woods previously introduced PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp at a monumental news conference for the golf organization late last month, his first appearance since returning from treatment. Woods has served as a leader on the Tour's Future Competition Committee, which he called a "privilege" during his brief introduction of Rolapp.

Woods must still make a court appearance for his DUI on Sept. 8.
